name: Classroom Observation Protocol for Undergraduate STEM
description: Observers mark which student and instructor activities happen in each 2-minute interval of a class session. The result describes how class time is spent; it is explicitly not a rating of teaching quality. Designed so faculty can use it reliably after a short training. Adapted from the Teaching Dimensions Observation Protocol (TDOP).

construct_mapping.note: Recorded by maintainers; awaiting governance committee review.

original_citation.text: Smith, M. K., Jones, F. H. M., Gilbert, S. L., & Wieman, C. E. (2013). The Classroom Observation Protocol for Undergraduate STEM (COPUS): A new instrument to characterize university STEM classroom practices. CBE-Life Sciences Education, 12(4), 618-627.

access.terms_summary: Codes and protocol may be reused with credit to Smith, Jones, Gilbert & Wieman (2013), for noncommercial use, under the same license (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0).

item_text_basis.evidence: The 2013 CBE-LSE article is released under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (https://www.compadre.org/portal/items/detail.cfm?ID=13381); UBC CWSEI lists its COPUS protocol summary as CC BY-NC 3.0 (https://cwsei.ubc.ca/node/1291).

versions.label: Version 1
versions.administration_minutes: Length of the class session; about 1.5 hours of observer training beforehand

response_format.notes: 25 codes; observers mark every code that occurs in each 2-minute interval.

scoring.notes: Percent of intervals in which each code occurred, usually shown as separate student and instructor charts. No composite score.

needs_check: The paper form also has an optional engagement rating; decide whether to model it as a third dimension.
Code descriptions should be taken from the CC-licensed article or CWSEI summary, and the item file marked CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.
Code split (13 student, 12 instructor) taken from the CHIRAL review of COPUS; confirm against Smith et al. (2013), Figure 1.
